critique_of_range_construction_peer: Range-C peer reaches CALL but at a softer 70/30 split and grants AdKd the 'prototypical semi-bluff raise candidate' label by structural blocker logic (A blocks AT, K blocks KT). The MW critique: this logic is sound HEADS-UP but breaks 3-way because (a) CO's range is structurally weighted toward holding KT/T9/T8/JT slowplays that hero's blockers do NOT remove enough of, and (b) the raise-to-bluff slice in MW is smaller than HU because two ranges must fold simultaneously. Their 30% raise frequency over-allocates AdKd to the bluff slice and under-discounts the CO sandwich problem they themselves cite as the modal-action driver.
critique_of_sonnet_split: RAISE camp (labellers 4, 5) anchors on (a) 'charges two opponents,' (b) 'isolates vs MP value,' (c) 'builds pot for nut-T hits,' (d) sizing aligned to solver 3-4x. The structural error: 'charges two opponents' inverts MW logic — a raise must FOLD both ranges' equity-realization hands to gain, but on QJ9 neither MP's overpair/Qx/sets nor CO's JT/T9/KT/two-pair fold to ~9bb. The raise charges hero's own equity-realization more than villains'. CALL camp (labellers 1, 2, 3) correctly identifies: 21% pot odds + nut-gutshot price + IP-closing realization + implied odds on T-runouts + dominated-by-3-bet risk. CALL camp's reasoning matches the MW framework.
critique_of_opus_tierup: Opus's RAISE-to-9bb verdict is the most coherent RAISE case but still fails the MW lens. Opus claims 48-52% raw equity vs MP's c-bet range — this is HU-style range modeling that ignores CO's range entirely in the equity calculation. The joint MP-c-bet-AND-CO-continue range has AdKd at ~30-35% raw, not ~50%. Opus also asserts the raise 'folds CO's capped continuance' — but CO's continuance on QJ9 is precisely the part that DOESN'T fold (JT/T9/QJ/sets/KT). Opus's nut-blocker count (any T = nuts) is correct, but the realization argument that flop-raise unlocks that equity is backwards: raising forfeits the cheap turn card that makes the T-equity priceable. RAISE NOT credible under MW lens.
revised_reasoning: MW framework gates the verdict on three tests: (1) does the raise charge BOTH villains' continuing ranges out of equity-realization? (2) does hero's hand carry made-class equity that wins when called by the joint continuing range? (3) does sandwich-geometry (player behind) penalize the raise? On all three, AdKd fails the RAISE test. Test 1: MP's 26% c-bet range continues with Qx+/JJ+/sets/two-pair/KT/AK/some Tx — almost none of which folds to ~9bb (the small c-bet was specifically a merged sizing that protects its range from folding). CO is range-capped (no AA/KK/AQs+) but DENSELY concentrated in JT/T9/T8/QJ/sets/KT — the exact part of CO's range that snap-continues vs a flop raise. Neither villain's bluff/air slice is large enough to make fold-equity the dominant raise-EV term in 3-way. Test 2: AdKd has zero made-class equity (no pair, no draw beyond the gutshot+BDFD). Vs the joint MP-continue × CO-continue range, hero is ~30-35% raw with 0.85 IP-closing realization. When the raise is called by both, hero plays a bloated pot at equity-deficit vs hands that have hero's gutshot drawing thin to non-board T's (and even the T can make a higher straight for CO when CO holds KT — which CO's flat range includes per labeller 4's chain). Test 3: CO acts behind on the raise, so squeeze/check-raise risk is non-zero. CO's slowplay frequency with sets/two-pair is real on this texture (CO flatted preflop to disguise these classes), and AdKd has no equity defense vs a CO check-raise. Counter to RAISE camp: 'charges two villains' inverts MW logic — the raise charges hero's equity-realization more than villains'. CALL clears all three tests: 21% pot odds covered by gutshot + BDFD + overcard equity; implied odds on nut-T runouts are substantial; CO's slowplays stay disguised and pay off; hero's range stays uncapped; the 3-bet-blowoff risk disappears. Verdict UNCHANGED: CALL, HIGH confidence.
